# About
Library was created as a wrapper for `taf.sw.dcap.rd` in order to make DCAP log collection in automated tests more accessible to everyone.

# How does it work?
Underlying structure of the library utilizes methods available in `taf.sw.dcap.rd`. 

Basic workflow: Start DCAP containers -> Add BTS to running local instance of DCAP server -> Start collecting logs
>__NOTE__
> DCAP is preinstalled to all UTE VMs starting from 24.01.2023.

DCAP uses **traces** in order to collect logs. You can choose whether you want one particular (i.e. scf, snapshot) or multiple logs collected within one trace.
For description of the available logs and trace settings, please refer to the official [DCAP TAF documentation](https://taf-sw-dcap-rd.docs.taf.ute.nsn-rdnet.net/en/latest/interfaces/interface.html#module-taf.sw.dcap.rd.interface)

After you started the trace, you might face 2 situations:
1. Download archive with results once the trace is finished (case for non-continuous logs)
2. Stop the trace and download the archive (case for continuous logs, i.e. syslog, IP capturing etc.)

>__WARNING__
> It's **impossible** to start multiple traces at once in DCAP. If you need to start a new one, you must stop a running one first.

>__NOTE__
> Restarting DCAP containers **has no effect** on a working instance of DCAP server. 

# Usage Examples

### 1. Use Case Example - Collect SCF (non-continuous log)
Complete example for collecting SCF.
```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource         taf/rfrl/utilities/dcap/dcap.robot

*** Keywords ***
DCAP Collect SCF from BTS
    [Arguments]         ${log_dir}     ${with_name}
    # Trace arguments are only accepted as lists
    ${bts_custom_profile}=            Create List     scf
    # Connection established in the beginning
    dcap.connect  
    # Start tracing the log
    ${trace_id}=       dcap.start_trace                 bts_custom_profile=${bts_custom_profile}
    # Wait for trace to stop running (for non-continuous logs)   
    dcap.wait_for_trace_running
    # Get archive with results from trace
    ${filepath}=       dcap.get_results                 trace_id=${trace_id}      log_dir=${log_dir}    
    ...                                                 with_name=${with_name}
    # Extra: Extact logfile from the archive
    ${log_filepath}=   dcap.extract_logfile_from_zip    path=${filepath}          log_name=scf
    ...                                                 collect_trace_logs=True   delete_zip=True
    [Return]           ${log_filepath}
```
__NOTE__
Method `extract_logfile_from_zip` helps you to extract log from the collected archive. Arguments:

- `path` - path to the collected archive

- `log_name` - Logs are stored in zip as: <...>_<log_name>.. Script looks for the file that contains specified log_name param.

- `collect_trace_logs` - also extracts DCAP tool logs that were generated during tracing process

- `delete_zip` - whether to delete initial archive

### 2. Use Case Example - Collect Syslog (continuous log)
Complete example for collecting syslog.
```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource         taf/rfrl/utilities/dcap/dcap.robot

*** Keywords ***
DCAP Collect Syslog from BTS
    [Arguments]         ${log_dir}     ${with_name}
    # Trace arguments are only accepted as lists
    ${gnb_custom_profile}=      Create List     condor5gSyslog
    # Connection established in the beginning
    dcap.connect  
    # Start tracing the log
    ${trace_id}=       dcap.start_trace                gnb_custom_profile=${gnb_custom_profile}
    # some logic here
    # Stop tracing (case for continuous logs)
    dcap.stop_trace                                    trace_id=${trace_id}
    # Get archive with results from trace
    ${filepath}=       dcap.get_results                trace_id=${trace_id}      log_dir=${log_dir}     
    ...                                                with_name=${with_name}
    # Extra: Extact logfile from the archive
    ${log_filepath}=   dcap.extract_logfile_from_zip   path=${filepath}          log_name=Syslog
    ...                                                collect_trace_logs=True   delete_zip=True
    [Return]           ${log_filepath}
```

### 3. Use Case Example - Test Suites
Complete suite example can be found here: [CRT_ASIK_Service_Account_on_RU_AEUD.robot](https://wrgitlab.int.net.nokia.com/RAN/robotws/-/blob/master/testsuite/Wroclaw/TRS/RAN_5G/regression/SBTS00/CRT_ASIK_Service_Account_on_RU_AEUD.robot)

Generally, suite template looks like this:
- Suite Setup -> Start DCAP, Add BTS to DCAP
- Test Setup + Test Teardown -> Collect necessary logs
- Suite Teardown -> Collect necessary logs

>__NOTE__
> The example below collects syslog during the test (start trace in test setup, collect results in test teardown).
> 
> *Keep in mind*: because of that, no other logs can be collected during the test using DCAP because syslog trace will block any attempts to start 
> a new trace before stopping the current one and exception will be raised.

Example:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource         taf/rfrl/utilities/dcap/dcap.robot

Suite Setup         Suite Setup
Suite Teardown      Suite Teardown

Test Setup          Test Setup  
Test Teardown       Test Teardown  

*** Test Cases ***
Test Case 1
    Log to console      test case 1
    
Test Case 2
    Log to console      test case 2
    
*** Keywords ***
Suite Setup
    dcap.Start DCAP on UTE VM 
    dcap.connect
    dcap.add_gnb
    
Suite Teardown
    dcap.DCAP Collect SCF from BTS              log_dir=results     with_name=suite_teardown_scf 
    dcap.DCAP Collect Snapshot from BTS         log_dir=results     with_name=suite_teardown_snapshot

Test Setup
    dcap.DCAP Collect SCF from BTS              log_dir=results     with_name=test_setup_scf 
    dcap.DCAP Collect Snapshot from BTS         log_dir=results     with_name=test_setup_snapshot
    Start Collecting Syslog from BTS        # NOTE:  since DCAP does not allow to run multiple traces as once, 
                                            #        this keyword should be the last one in setup

Test Teardown
    Stop Collecting Syslog from BTS         # NOTE: Stop syslog trace firstly, then collect other logs
    dcap.DCAP Collect SCF from BTS              log_dir=results     with_name=test_teardown_scf 
    dcap.DCAP Collect Snapshot from BTS         log_dir=results     with_name=test_teardown_snapshot
    
Start Collecting Syslog from BTS   
    ${gnb_custom_profile}=    Create List                     condor5gSyslog    
    ${syslog_trace_id}=       dcap.start_trace                gnb_custom_profile=${gnb_custom_profile}
    Set Test Variable    ${syslog_trace_id}

Stop Collecting Syslog from BTS   
    [Arguments]         ${log_dir}     ${with_name}
    dcap.stop_trace                                    trace_id=${syslog_trace_id}
    # Get archive with results from trace    
    ${filepath}=       dcap.get_results                trace_id=${syslog_trace_id}      log_dir=${log_dir}     
    ...                                                with_name=${with_name}
    # Extra: Extact logfile from the archive    
    ${log_filepath}=   dcap.extract_logfile_from_zip   path=${filepath}          log_name=Syslog                                                
    ...                                                collect_trace_logs=True   delete_zip=True    
    [Return]           ${log_filepath}
```
